title: Sample true nonlinear endpoints with a paid polynomial interaction budget
statement: Let M=sum w_i*x0_vi, w*=min w_i, and Lambda=sum_(r:|y_r|>=2) kappa_r V^(1-|y_r|)*(M/w*)^|y_r|. Conservation and factorial bounds make this a uniform rational bound on total nonlinear rate in every actual state. For every fixed q>=1, the original full endpoint has an unconditional entire-TV sampler with every-run polynomial(B+epsilon^-1) resources whenever mu=Lambda*T<=(1+B+epsilon^-1)^q. Use a state-independent proposal Poisson clock Lambda, exact nonlinear-channel/vertex thinning q_rv(x)/Lambda, and accepted source-unary family evolution between proposals. Truncate proposals at J=ceil(6mu)+ceil(log2(16/epsilon)); tail<=epsilon/16. Sample the normalized finite rational count weights mu^k/k!, then sorted dyadic uniforms in[0,T]. Bound unary/diffusion exit rate QY<=(M/w*)*(sum_source-unary kappa+(n-1)max delta). Interval error is<=QY*h; precision 2^-b<=epsilon/[128(J+1)^2(1+QY*T)] plus allocated count/timestamp/collision/menu/family errors pays unconditional TV. All jumps use enabled original transitions, and null proposals preserve support; every output lies in the actual original class. Lambda=0 or T=0 uses the accepted deterministic/unary cases. This permits polynomially many substantial interactions, rather than discarding them; no arbitrary-budget acceleration follows.
